findings.title: Duplicate asset inputs are preserved, producing duplicate rows, state queries and checkout attempts
evidence: TurboMCPAssetResolver.cpp:182-206 SplitList splits on comma/pipe, trims and culls empty parts, but never deduplicates.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:252-320 loops every input and creates one row/GetState call per duplicate.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:443-527 Checkout loops every row and can issue FCheckOut once per duplicate.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:390-404 prints assets: N and one 1-based row per input, so duplicates inflate the count.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Passing the same resolved asset twice produces two rows; with a provider it produces two GetState(ForceUpdate) calls and can issue two FCheckOut operations for one file. No duplicate warning or deduplication exists. Ordering is preserved and empty separators are silently culled.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py uses exactly two distinct fixtures and checks len(rows)==2; it never sends a duplicate or separator-only input.

findings.title: Checkout executes against the plan state without revalidation, post-operation read-back or aggregate outcome
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:293 reads state once; Checkout at :410-530 never calls GetState before or after Provider.Execute.

Checkout skips refused rows and rows without readable state first (:455-460); the checked-out/added skip is only in the UsesCheckout()==true branch (:473-488). On a no-checkout provider a readable checked-out/added row still issues FCheckOut. CanCheckout() false does not prevent the attempt.

The result section (:494-522) reports the operation's ECommandResult and messages only. The result fields bAttempted/bSucceeded/ProviderAnswer in TurboMCPSourceControl.h:101-109 are not populated by this path.
The per-asset loop continues after failures; there is no rollback, aggregate count or partial-success summary.
Preview and Edit each call Plan separately (:39-50); sharing the Plan function does not share a state snapshot across calls, so state changes between calls can change the answer.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A stale plan can attempt a checkout on a changed file or, in the UsesCheckout()==true branch, skip a file whose plan state says checked out/added even though that state is stale. On a no-checkout provider, readable checked-out/added rows are not skipped: the operation is still issued. ECommandResult::Succeeded is the provider operation result, not a verified checkout; no post-state read proves the lock. Partial multi-asset results have no aggregate or rollback.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py only exercises Git no-op and no-provider/Perforce-unavailable paths; it never observes a successful checkout or reads state back. test-vcs-write.py tests write tools, not this checkout tool.

findings.title: Checked-out-by-other, non-null unknown and read-only distinctions are not surfaced as structured state

The plan prints UsesLocalReadOnlyState at :238,363 but does not inspect a file's read-only attribute; CanCheckout is the only structured read-only-adjacent signal.
findings.observed_source_behavior: Read/Preview state rows cannot distinguish checked out by another user, a genuinely unknown non-null state, or a filesystem read-only asset except through provider text or CanCheckout. The declaration says it reports 'whether it is checked out here', which is true, but the broader state question is not structured.

findings.title: Preview and Edit branch on UsesCheckout and readable state in different orders
evidence: TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:145-177 AddAssetLines checks !InPlan.bUsesCheckout first; its bStateRead check is at :163.
TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:455-488 Checkout checks !Row.bStateRead first (:455-460) and the no-checkout branch at :473-479.
For a resolved row with no refusal, UsesCheckout() false and a null state, Preview says the provider is still asked, while Edit prints NOT ATTEMPTED and continues.

The already-checked-out/added skip in Checkout is an else-if after the no-op branch (:481-487); with UsesCheckout() false and a readable state, Edit still issues FCheckOut even when bCheckedOut/bAdded are true.
Preview and Edit call Plan separately (:39-50); the branch mismatch exists on the same plan input and does not require a state change between calls.

The readable-state/no-checkout row is not a skip: Edit still calls the provider even if the state says checked out or added. The branch order is the defect; plan refusals and operation outcomes are separate.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs.py has no null-state/UsesCheckout-false case and no readable checked-out/added no-checkout case; it only sees Git readable states and a no-provider refusal.

findings.title: Source-control preflight runs before per-asset write eligibility
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:405-406 calls FTurboMCPSourceControlWrite::EnsureCheckedOut(Plan(Parts), 'E-SAVE') before the save loop, which begins at :419.
The loop's dirty check is :432-437, package lookup :439-449, asset load :456-467, and the no-thumbnail /Game refusal :479-491. All of these happen after Plan/GetState/EnsureCheckedOut.

TurboMCPSourceControlWrite.cpp:254-343 builds one row per input and calls the base VCS Plan; :371-460 issues Provider.Execute(FCheckOut) for every row the plan allows. TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:269-317 verifies only that a file exists and reads provider state; it does not probe the local read-only attribute.
TurboMCPAssetResolver.cpp:182-206 preserves duplicates, so duplicate inputs repeat the state operation and can repeat the checkout operation.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A clean asset, a package the selected tool will refuse (non-/Game for EditTurboMCPSaveWithoutThumbnail), an object that later fails to load, and a duplicate input all receive the source-control preflight before the code decides whether to write. A call that reports 'unchanged: nothing to save' can still have issued GetState(ForceUpdate) and FCheckOut. The preflight is a report, not a gate, which is D-57 behavior; the defect is its placement before write eligibility.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs-write.py:423-449 covers a brand-new asset with no provider (the preflight refuses because there is no file), and :623-636 covers E-SAVE under Git (the preflight is the failed no-op). findings.title: E-SAVE performs a second, unreported checkout inside the editor save path
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:405-406 issues the tool's FCheckOut before the loop; :516 then calls UEditorAssetLibrary::SaveLoadedAsset.
EditorAssetSubsystem.cpp:1290-1310 forwards to UEditorLoadingAndSavingUtils::SavePackages; FileHelpers.cpp:6019-6022 calls InternalCheckoutAndSavePackages.

The appended block is built only from the tool's own Plan/EnsureCheckedOut (TurboMCPSourceControlWrite.cpp:345-460); it has no field for the engine's second pass.

The engine may decide the file is already checked out and perform no second provider FCheckOut, but the path and its result are outside the tool's report. A new asset that the tool's plan refuses for having no file can still be marked for add by the engine after the save. The result block cannot distinguish the two passes.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs-write.py:430-449 checks only the tool's appended block and the save count; :713-732 checks that EnsureCheckedOut is called. No test counts provider operations or shows the engine's checkout pass; no live provider is available.

findings.title: The direct write does not preserve E-SAVE's package semantics beyond the thumbnail
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:479-495 always builds a /Game relative path with FPackageName::GetAssetPackageExtension(); it has no ContainsMap/GetMapPackageExtension branch. :533 calls UPackage::SavePackage directly.

The engine's own package save chooses GetMapPackageExtension for a world package (FileHelpers.cpp:3747-3775) and SaveAsset calls SaveExternalPackages before the write (:1318-1332). The tool header at TurboMCPToolsets.h:1623-1647 describes the tool as the same save minus the thumbnail and says everything else is E-SAVE's behavior.

A newly written file is not marked for add by this tool. A loaded asset that E-SAVE's registered-asset check would reject can still reach the direct SavePackage call. Whether UPackage::SavePackage refuses or writes the mismatched map filename is not runtime-verified; either result is not E-SAVE-equivalent.

findings.title: The direct write still executes asset PreSave/PostSave code
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:523-533 calls UPackage::SavePackage(Package, AssetObject, Filename, SaveArgs) with the asset object.

SavePackage2.cpp:4050-4060 calls PreSavePackage and CallPreSaveRoot on the asset; :4117-4129 calls CallPostSaveRoot and PostSavePackage; the package path serializes objects and can invoke their Serialize overrides.
WidgetBlueprint.cpp:705-713 overrides UWidgetBlueprint::PreSave and clears/updates the generated class widget tree. This is asset code, not thumbnail drawing.

findings.observed_source_behavior: EditTurboMCPSaveWithoutThumbnail skips the editor thumbnail step but still runs SavePackage's PreSave/PreSaveRoot/PostSaveRoot/PostSave and serialization hooks on the asset and its objects. It cannot be described as a save that does not run the asset's own code. Whether a particular project override has external effects is asset-specific and unverified.
findings.existing_assertions: test-save-thumbnail-option.py:231-236 checks result text saying the design-time code did not run for a draw. It does not use an asset with an observable PreSave/PreSaveRoot override, and no test observes asset code during the direct write.

findings.title: Per-input counters are not per-package write outcomes
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:419-428 loops over Parts and increments SavedCount/NoChangeCount/FailedCount per input; :553-558 increments SavedCount for each input whose package is clean after the save; :624-639 prints those input counts.
E-SAVE's SaveLoadedAsset saves the package (EditorAssetSubsystem.cpp:1305-1309) and can save external packages (FileHelpers.cpp:1321). The direct path saves one package (TurboMCPCompile.cpp:533).
SplitList preserves duplicates (TurboMCPAssetResolver.cpp:182-206), so the same package can appear more than once; the first row can save it and the later row then reports 'had no changes'.
findings.observed_source_behavior: With two assets in one package, the first row may save the package and the second row reports no changes: the headline 'saved 1 of 2 asset(s)' does not say that both assets were in the package that was written. Duplicate inputs have the same shape. E-SAVE can write external packages that are never named in the counts. When several inputs fail against one package, the count reports several failures for one package write. There is no package result, unattempted list, or explicit partial outcome.
findings.existing_assertions: test-save-thumbnail-option.py saves one asset per call. test-vcs-write.py repeats E-SAVE on the same asset in separate calls but does not pass duplicates in one call or use a multi-asset package. No test asserts a package-level saved/failed/unattempted map.

findings.title: Mechanism narration is not conditioned on the observed outcome
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:553-561 prints 'thumbnail/design-time work: ran through the editor's save path' for every successful E-SAVE asset. The engine generates a thumbnail only when the cached thumbnail is missing or dirty and not in automation (UnrealEdSrv.cpp:438-446,478-491); it may only load/keep an existing thumbnail.

The Widget Blueprint explanation at TurboMCPCompile.cpp:591-601 is outside the success/failure branch. On a failed no-thumbnail widget save, it still says 'the package was written directly, so the engine's thumbnail step did not run for this save, and this widget's design-time code did not run for a draw.' The failure branch is :563-579.
The success branch at :553-561 is the only place that says the write happened; the widget block does not consult bStillDirty.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A failed EditTurboMCPSaveWithoutThumbnail on a Widget Blueprint can print both 'is still unsaved after two attempts' and 'the package was written directly'. A successful E-SAVE can say thumbnail/design-time work ran when no draw was needed, because the code does not observe the thumbnail cache or the renderer. The widget sentence is true only when a draw actually ran; the code only knows that the editor save path was selected.
findings.existing_assertions: test-save-thumbnail-option.py asserts the success strings at :181, :191-197 and :231-235. Its own header says a thumbnail draw cannot be observed in logs. No test forces a failed no-thumbnail widget save or a fresh cached-thumbnail E-SAVE.

findings.title: No read-only preflight and no structured read-only failure cause
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:50-74 WriteRefusalReason checks GIsEditor, GEditor, PIE and simulate only; it does not check the package file's read-only attribute.

The VCS plan used for preflight checks file existence and provider state but not IFileManager::IsReadOnly (TurboMCPSourceControl.cpp:269-317; TurboMCPSourceControlWrite.h:96-153). A checkout may clear read-only, but the tool does not re-probe after checkout.

The save failure branch at TurboMCPCompile.cpp:563-579 collapses the engine result and dirty flag into 'still unsaved after two attempts' and guesses 'The asset may be read only, or another program may hold the file.' The direct path has no file-attribute check either.
findings.observed_source_behavior: A read-only package with no usable provider is attempted twice and reported with a speculative cause. A provider checkout that succeeds but leaves the file read-only is not distinguished from any other save failure. A provider checkout that fails is not allowed to gate the write, so the save can still fail on read-only and the report does not identify which condition held.
findings.existing_assertions: test-vcs-write.py has no read-only case; it uses no-provider and Git refusals. Tests/acceptance.json F08 ('Force save refusal on an owned read-only scratch package') is not_mapped at :981-994. No test forces a read-only file or a checkout that succeeds without clearing read-only.

findings.title: Saved means the dirty flag cleared, not verified persistence
evidence: TurboMCPCompile.cpp:548-558 decides success from Package->IsDirty(). The returned bSaved is used only to choose the failure wording at :568-570.
UPackage::SavePackage clears the dirty flag only after ESavePackageResult::Success (SavePackage2.cpp:3599-3607). That is an in-process engine success signal, not a readback of the file or a reload.

Neither tool reloads the package or compares its contents after the write. test-struct.py:287-309 checks only that the file exists and contains field bytes; test-save-thumbnail-option.py:210-252 checks the dirty list. Tests/acceptance.json F07 ('Save owned fixture, unload/reload it') is not_mapped at :967-980.
findings.observed_source_behavior: The output 'package write: saved' and 'changed: saved N of M asset(s)' claims a successful package write on the basis of an in-memory dirty flag. No durable persistence, file-byte verification, reload or multi-file atomicity is established. ARC05 requires a successful engine write result and durable verification appropriate to the path; this checkpoint can confirm the engine success signal, not the durable result.
findings.existing_assertions: No current engine suite reloads a saved fixture and compares contents. test-struct.py checks file existence and bytes; test-save-thumbnail-option.py checks the dirty list after 14 seconds. F07 remains not_mapped.
